summary: Johann Gottfried Eichhorn worked in religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne (~1770–1774), later serving as professor of Oriental languages at Jena (~1775–1788) and Professor of Philosophy at Göttingen (~1788–1827).

Johann Gottfried Ludwig Kosegarten was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Greifswald (~1808–1812). He held academic posts at the University of Jena (~1817–1824) and as a professor at the University of Greifswald (~1824–1850).

Johann Wilhelm Andreas Pfaff, active in Indology, studied at the University of Tübingen (~1791–1795). He subsequently held positions at the Imperial University of Dorpat (~1803–1809), University of Würzburg (~1815–1818), and University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1818–1835).

Johanna Engelberta van Lohuizen-de Leeuw worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at Utrecht University (~1939–1949), she held posts at the University of Groningen (~1951–1959) and as Director of South Asian Archaeology at the University of Amsterdam (1959–1983).

Johanna Narten worked in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. She studied at Saarland University (~1951–1956) and held an academic post at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1971–1995).

Johannes Beltz specializes in Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD by 1999 through studies at the University of Lausanne and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under supervisors Johannes Bronkhorst and Marie-Louise Reiniche.

Johannes Bronkhorst worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, Savitribai Phule Pune University under S. D. Joshi (PhD ~1976–1979), and Leiden University (~1979–1980), later becoming a professor at the University of Lausanne in 1987.

Johannes Gildemeister worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen under Heinrich Ewald (~1832–1834) and Bonn under G. W. Freytag and Christian Lassen (~1834–1838), holding professorships at the University of Marburg (~1845–1859) and University of Bonn (~1859–1890).

Indologist Johannes Hertel earned his PhD from Leipzig University (~1893–1897). He held a post at Lessing-Gymnasium Döbeln (~1898–1920, attested professor 1927) and later held the chair of Indian philology at Leipzig University (~1920–1937).

Indologist Johannes Klatt studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1869–1873) and under Albrecht Weber (~1872–1873). From around 1874 to 1892, he served as custos of the Indian department at the Berlin State Library.

Johannes Nobel specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Heinrich Lüders (~1908–1911) and held posts at Berlin (~1915–1927) and as a professor at the University of Marburg (~1927–1955, attested 1957).

Johannes Rahder worked in Indology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Utrecht University (~1915–1926), he held posts at Utrecht (1930–1931), Leiden (1931–1946), the University of Hawaii (1946–1947), and Yale University (1961–1962).

Linguist and Indologist Johannes Schmidt studied at Jena under August Schleicher (~1862–1865) and Bonn under Albrecht Weber (1865–1866). He held posts at Bonn (~1868–1873), Graz (~1873–1876), and as a professor at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1876–1901).

Johannes Schneider works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He held a post at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1999) and served on the editorial board of the Deshana Institute of Buddhist and Allied Studies (attested 2021).

Johannes Schubert specialized in Tibetology and Sinology, studying under August Conrady (~1920–1925) and August Hermann Francke (~1923–1928). He held a post at Ahnenerbe (~1939–1945) and was later professor of Tibetan at Leipzig University (~1952–1961).

John A. Ardussi works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed an MA under Turrell V. Wylie, earned a PhD at the Australian National University (attested 1977), and served as a research team member at the CNRS.

John A. Brinkman is a historian and archaeologist. He held appointments at the University of Chicago (~1963–2004) and served as a professor at the Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures (~1964–2004).

John Allan worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1900–1905) and Leipzig University (~1905–1907), later serving as Keeper of the Department of Coins and Medals at the British Museum (~1931–1949, attested 1951).

John Avery was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Amherst, Tübingen, Berlin, and under William Dwight Whitney (~1866–1869). He served as Professor of Greek at Grinnell College (1870–1877) and Bowdoin College (1877).

John Borthwick Gilchrist worked in linguistics and Indology. Educated at Royal High School, George Heriot's School, and the University of Edinburgh, he served in the East India Company (~1782–1804), Fort William College (~1800–1804), and East India Company College (1806).
